title: Equivalence testing with data-dependent and post-hoc equivalence margins
summary: Equivalence testing compares the hypothesis that an effect $μ$ is large against the alternative that it is negligible. Here, `large' is classically expressed as being larger than some `equivalence margin' $Δ$. A longstanding problem is that this margin must be specified but can rarely be objectively justified in practice. We lay the foundation for an alternative paradigm, arguing to instead report a data-dependent margin $\widehatΔ_α$ that bounds the true effect $μ$ with probability $1 - α$.
